Plot traits on the tree: phylomorphospace or traitgram

Source: R/mv_plots.R
plot_traits.Rd

Draws simulated traits with the tree that generated them. With two traits, a phylomorphospace: the tips and internal nodes in the plane of the two traits, joined by the branches of the tree. With one trait, a traitgram: the trait against time from the root. Branches are coloured by selective regime, with the change of colour at the point of each shift in a mapped history.

Usage

plot_traits(
  x,
  tree = NULL,
  traits = c(1, 2),
  regimes = NULL,
  colours = NULL,
  tip_labels = FALSE,
  legend = TRUE,
  point_size = 1.8,
  linewidth = 0.7,
  ...,
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Traits of the tips from trait_ou(): a matrix with one row per tip, named by tip label.

tree

The tree of x, a phylo object; or NULL to draw only the tips.

traits

The two columns of x to draw (names or numbers), or one for a traitgram.

regimes

Regimes of the branches, as in trait_ou(): a vector in the cladewise order of the edges (from paint_regimes()) or a tree with a mapped history (class simmap, from trait_mk()). NULL draws every branch in one colour.

colours

Colours of the regimes, named by regime or in the order of the sorted regimes; one colour when there are no regimes.

tip_labels

Should the tips be labelled?

legend

Draw the legend of the regimes?

point_size

Size of the tips.

linewidth

Width of the branches.

labels, ...

Deprecated: labels is now tip_labels; graphical arguments of base graphics are no longer used (modify the ggplot object instead).

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The values of the internal nodes are those kept by trait_ou() in the attribute nodes, so the branches show the simulated path between nodes, not a reconstruction. Without that attribute, only the tips are drawn.

See also

trait_ou(), rate_matrix() and plot.rate_matrix().

Other species traits: arrival_ages(), as_herodotools(), food_web_rates(), history_rates(), paint_regimes(), partner_turnover(), plot.rate_matrix(), plot_rates(), rate_matrix(), region_pool(), species_traits(), tip_history_metrics(), trait_bm(), trait_mk(), trait_ou(), trait_rates(), turnover_rates()

Examples

set.seed(2)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(30)
habitat <- trait_mk(tr, q = 0.5, states = c("forest", "open"))
r <- rate_matrix(c(1, 1), correlation = list(forest = 0.8, open = -0.8),
                 constraint = "variance")
x <- trait_ou(habitat, sigma2 = r, regimes = habitat)
plot_traits(x, habitat, regimes = habitat)

# traitgram of the first trait
plot_traits(x, habitat, traits = 1, regimes = habitat)
